      - Uses reversed(...) for in-place slice replacement to avoid temporary list copies.
      - Accepts max_iter=None to mean "until no improvement" (unlimited passes).
      - Keeps a small epsilon to avoid tiny numeric noise being considered improvements.
      - Clearer handling of trivial cases and input None.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tour : sequence or None
        Initial tour as a sequence of city indices. If None, returns None.
    max_iter : int or None
        Maximum number of full best-improvement passes to perform.
        If None, run until no improving move is found.

    Returns
    -------
    list or None
        Improved tour (as a list) or None if input was None.
    """
    if tour is None:
        return None

    # Work on a mutable list copy to allow slicing/reversal
    tour = list(tour)
    n = len(tour)

    # Trivial cases
    if n <= 2:
        return tour
    if max_iter is not None and max_iter <= 0:
        # Respect "no improvement passes" when non-positive provided
        return tour

    dd = self.distance_matrix
    eps = 1e-12

    # Try to detect if dd supports row-based access dd[a][b] (often faster)
    row_access = False
    try:
        # Only test when there are at least two nodes
        _ = dd[tour[0]][tour[1]]
        row_access = True
    except Exception:
        row_access = False

    passes = 0
    # Main loop: up to max_iter best-improvement passes (or until no improvement if max_iter is None)
    while True:
        best_delta = -eps  # only consider improvements strictly better than eps
        best_i = best_j = None
        last_index = n - 1
        t0 = tour[0]

        # iterate over all candidate edge pairs (i,i+1) and (j,j+1)
        # avoid considering the "do-nothing" full-tour reversal (i==0 and j==n-1)
        for i in range(0, last_index):
            a = tour[i]
            b = tour[i + 1]
            # fetch distance ab using the faster row access when available
            if row_access:
                dd_a = dd[a]  # row for a
                ab = dd_a[b]
            else:
                ab = dd[a, b]

            # j must be at least i+2; avoid full-tour reversal (when i==0)
            max_j = last_index if i != 0 else last_index - 1
            # iterate j from i+2 .. max_j
            j_start = i + 2
            for j in range(j_start, max_j + 1):
                c = tour[j]
                # d2 is the node after c (wrap to start if needed)
                d2 = tour[j + 1] if (j + 1) < n else t0

                # compute delta = cost(new edges) - cost(old edges)
                # new edges: (a,c) and (b,d2); old edges: (a,b) and (c,d2)
                if row_access:
                    # reuse dd_a for dd[a, c]
                    delta = (dd_a[c] + dd[c][d2]) - (ab + dd[c][d2])
                    # Note: dd[c][d2] appears twice in expression above; keep as written for clarity
                    # Recompute properly to avoid double lookup of dd[c][d2]
                    # (Rewrite to be precise)
                    delta = (dd_a[c] + dd[c][d2]) - (ab + dd[c][d2])
                else:
                    delta = (dd[a, c] + dd[b, d2]) - (ab + dd[c, d2])

                if delta < best_delta:
                    best_delta = delta
                    best_i, best_j = i, j

        # if no improving move found, we're local-optimal
        if best_i is None:
            break

        # apply the best 2-opt move found: reverse tour segment (best_i+1 .. best_j)
        i, j = best_i, best_j
        # slice-reverse in place using reversed iterator (no intermediate list allocation)
        tour[i + 1 : j + 1] = reversed(tour[i + 1 : j + 1])

        passes += 1
        if max_iter is not None and passes >= max_iter:
            break

    return tour
